heading: Late MLPs suppress the most likely token less after earlier components are ablated
definition: late MLP layers downregulate the maximum-likelihood token, and this erasure shrinks when earlier components are ablated.
summary: The finding for whole layers rests on the original Chinchilla 7B study. One independent preprint supports an analogous response in selected neurons when swapping activations between contrasting inputs (contrastive swaps), without testing whole-layer effects.

suggested_status.by_scale: 1-10B: R2 for the selected-neuron, contrastive-swap analogue in Llama, Gemma, Qwen and Mistral instruct models (arXiv:2610.02173#R1–R4); the checker also confirms base-checkpoint evidence in Appendix H, Figures 17–20, omitted from the extracted rows. R0 for the layer-level ablation statement as written (arXiv:2307.15771#R4). Toy, <1B, 10-100B, >100B: no test recorded (counts: versions.V2.studies_by_size has only '1-10B').
suggested_status.reason: counts: versions.V2.studies_tested = 2; versions.V2.original_sources_linked identifies arXiv:2307.15771 as the original. Its Chinchilla 7B baseline reports reduced MLP erasure after attention-layer resample ablation (arXiv:2307.15771#R4). The independent selected-neuron analogue is supported under contrastive swaps on binary verdict margins (arXiv:2610.02173#R1, arXiv:2610.02173#R2, arXiv:2610.02173#R3, arXiv:2610.02173#R4). Qwen's opposition shrinking at ×1 supports V2; disappearance or reversal is not required (arXiv:2610.02173#R5, arXiv:2610.02173#R6). Whole-layer effects remain untested by that study, rather than a demonstrated limits_scope result. The recorded versions.V2.verdicts.limits_scope.studies = 1 reflects the label the checker rejects. Appendix H, Figures 17–20, extends neuron recruitment to matched base checkpoints in these families; versions.V2.studies_by_stage and versions.V2.coverage_by_operation.patching.by_stage omit this evidence. Independence is based on counts: versions.V2.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original = 0, not independently established by the paper. Both studies are recorded as preprints (versions.V2.tested_by_review_class.preprint = 2), with versions.V2.tested_with_code = 0. R2 applies to the neuron analogue; the layer-level statement retains only its original baseline.
suggested_status.open_questions: (1) Would a different group resample- or mean-ablating attention layers find whole late-MLP-layer erasure of the maximum-likelihood token shrinking? A yes, in any family, would make the layer-level statement R2; a clear failed replication would move it to C. (2) Does ×1 shrinkage generalize beyond the selected neurons and binary verdict task (arXiv:2610.02173#R5, arXiv:2610.02173#R6)? (3) Does whole-layer erasure reduction hold in base and instruct models, and does either the layer or neuron result hold below 1B or at 10B and above? Appendix H already supplies base-checkpoint neuron evidence. (4) Is there public code for either test?

source.title: The Hydra Effect: Emergent Self-repair in Language Model Computations
source.authors: Tom McGrath; Matthew Rahtz; János Kramár; Vladimir Mikulik; S. Legg

original_result.setup: The authors replaced attention-layer outputs with outputs from different prompts (resample ablation) in Chinchilla 7B and measured MLP effects on Counterfact contexts.
original_result.result: Late MLPs lowered the most likely token's logit, and this suppression weakened when attention layers promoting that token were ablated. At layer 23, almost all of this change came from MLPs that suppress the token (erasure MLPs).
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: Selected MLP neurons suppressed correct answers less, then supported them, as earlier components were removed.
Qwen’s L27.n13033 showed reduced opposition but still opposed the correct answer at ×1.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: Layer-level late-MLP erasure under ablation of earlier components, tested by anyone other than the original. The only removal (ablation) test on V2 is the original's Chinchilla 7B run. The other study swaps neurons rather than ablating them, and looks at single neurons rather than layers. Its measurements concern selected neurons with truth-token poles on a binary verdict margin; featured neurons are late in Gemma, Qwen and Mistral and mid-late in Llama. Whole-layer effects under those swaps are also untested.
untested.basis: arXiv:2610.02173 'untested parts of V2' line; selected-neuron measurements: arXiv:2610.02173#R5 and arXiv:2610.02173#R6; original layer-level baseline: arXiv:2307.15771#R4. checks/checks.json, arXiv:2610.02173, V2.against[0] confirms whole-layer erasure is untested rather than a demonstrated limitation. counts: versions.V2.coverage_by_operation.removal.studies = 1, with by_family showing only 'other or not stated' (the original's Chinchilla); versions.V2.coverage_by_operation.patching.studies = 1.

wording_issues.issue: The non-original evidence concerns selected single neurons with truth-token poles. In Llama-3-8B-Instruct the featured neuron is mid-late. Whole-layer effects are untested in that study, rather than shown to fail. The original measures layer-level MLP effects in Chinchilla 7B.

arXiv:2610.02173 measures an erased margin (nats) on a binary True/False verdict, with neurons opposing the correct verdict, not the maximum-likelihood token's logit. The original (R4) measures the MLP effect on the maximum-likelihood token.

The non-original test removes the upstream core by contrastive swap across a dose ladder, not by ablation (untested-parts line). The verdict fix equates only the x1 dose with an opposite-class resample. The upstream components it swaps are MLP neurons (cores such as L18.n11065), while the original resample-ablates attention layers.

method_sensitivity.factor: Dose of the upstream intervention (x1 vs x2 vs x4)
method_sensitivity.what: For Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct L27.n13033 under the joint core swap L22.n13149 + L24.n14758, clean erased margins are -2.86 / -2.88 nats (true / false class), shrinking to -0.50 / -0.51 nats at x1 (paired t = 15 each) and reversing to +2.93 / +3.22 nats at x2 (paired t = 116 / 109). The x1 swap is equivalent to resampling the matched opposite-class partner; x2 is beyond the on-manifold window. The x1 shrinkage supports V2 despite residual opposition. Qwen's net +8.7 nats endpoint is at x4, outside that window. Mistral L31.n8773 already contributes positively on both classes at x1; Figure 14 reports recruitment in every panel by x2, not this neuron's first crossing at x2. The study's method-sensitivity line says the response saturates beyond full inversion.

method_sensitivity.factor: Model and single vs joint core
method_sensitivity.what: Net erased-margin swing differs by model: Llama-3-8B-Instruct with a single core goes -0.10 -> +0.25 nats, while Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct with joint cores goes -5.7 -> +8.7 nats. Reported net contributions also cross zero and turn positive at the final plotted doses in Gemma and Mistral; some endpoints lie beyond the on-manifold window. The study's method-sensitivity line says responses differ by model, direction and dose, and that joint-core interventions can recruit more than single-core ones.

method_sensitivity.factor: Network depth of the ablated layer (original source, described as baseline)
method_sensitivity.what: In Chinchilla 7B, almost all of the response occurs in erasure MLPs at layer 23 (R4), and the about-70% restoration figure is for middle layers (R5). The original's method-sensitivity line says direct and compensatory effects correlate well mainly at intermediate layers. Early layers have large total but little direct effect. The direct-versus-compensatory slope is below 1 past layer 13 (R3), indicating incomplete compensation.
